name: Bosnia and Herzegovina

findings.summary: Huawei was contracted to deploy Telekom Srpske's UMTS/HSPA 3G radio network and packet-switched core, using SingleRAN equipment designed to be upgradable to later generations.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Huawei, so prc. Value undisclosed. Pre-2020 and still_current not confirmed: whether Huawei still supplies m:tel's 4G (launched 2019) radio/core was not established. Both trade-press items likely derive from a single Huawei release, so corroboration is formally met but thin. m:tel is Republika Srpska-based but holds a national licence, hence scale national.

findings.summary: Ericsson Nikola Tesla signed an HRK 34m frame agreement to expand HT Eronet's 800/1800 MHz LTE network across Bosnia, including integration and training; Ericsson is the operator's sole radio-access vendor, with 5G-ready equipment.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third. Tier 3 because it is a signed vendor supply contract with value and counterparty, though styled a frame agreement (tier 2 is arguable). US$5.2m is SeeNews's conversion (about EUR 4.6m). Pre-2020; current vendor status not re-confirmed.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska; City of Istočno Sarajevo
findings.summary: The Republika Srpska interior ministry reported a city video-surveillance system of more than 230 cameras in Istočno Sarajevo, built by its ICT administration, which won a Dahua 2019 regional best-project award.

sources.publisher: Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc on the inference that the cameras are Dahua equipment, implied by the vendor award but not stated outright on the page. Entity-level actor. Operational per the ministry; current status not re-confirmed.

findings.local_actor: City of Banja Luka; Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska
findings.summary: RFE/RL reported 265 of a planned 325 Dahua cameras already installed in Banja Luka's smart-city project, and that the Republika Srpska interior ministry bought 139 Dahua cameras in 2023 for about US$47,000.
findings.analyst_inference: Date is the article date; install start not given. Tier 4 because rollout is under way but incomplete. The US$47k figure refers only to the 139-camera ministry purchase, so values left null. The article also notes Hikvision purchases by Canton 10 police and rising Chinese recording-equipment imports (US$3.4m 2018 to US$5.4m 2023). Entity-level actors.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Interior of Sarajevo Canton
findings.summary: Sarajevo Canton police bought 200 Hytera body cameras with management software for about EUR 200,000 through local supplier MIBO Komunikacije; a traffic-police pilot began in July 2024. The ministry said procurement law did not let it exclude the bidder.
findings.analyst_inference: Hytera is a partly state-owned Chinese vendor supplying device firmware, so prc. Not a reversal: no exclusion occurred. US$222k is RFE/RL's conversion. Cantonal (Federation) actor.
